title: Finite Tor amplitude for closed support
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $T,Z$ be schemes, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be its quasi-compact complementary open immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Work in the ordinary derived categories of constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with $Rj_*$ the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $Ri^!$ the ambient right adjoint to $i_*$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Let $a,b$ be integers and let $c\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose $R^qj_*M=0$ for every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ and every $q>c$, and suppose every $R^qj_*$ takes constructible $A$-module sheaves to constructible $A$-module sheaves. If $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude], then $Ri^!K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in $[a,b+c+1]$.

proof.text: The diagonal of an open immersion is an isomorphism, hence quasi-compact, so $j$ is quasi-separated. Apply [lem-exc-direct-image-coproducts] with the finite commutative ring $A$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and the stated nonnegative bound $c$. It gives preservation by $Rj_*$ of every set-indexed coproduct, in particular of countable coproducts as required in Step 5.

Put $Q=Ri^!K$ and $d=b+c+1$. Taking the test sheaf $A_T$ in the definition [def-kun-tor-amplitude] shows that $K$ has cohomology in $[a,b]$, since $K\otimes_A^L A_T=K$. If $a>b$, these cohomology sheaves all vanish, so $K=0$ in the derived category, and $Ri^!K=0$ has the asserted properties; hence assume $a\leq b$. Apply the constructible clause of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] to $K$ with the assumed vanishing and constructibility of all $R^qj_*$. Thus $Q$ is bounded constructible, with cohomology in $[a,d]$. This establishes constructibility before any tensor comparison or residue-field test on $Q$.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: constructibility is lem-exc-closed-amplitude

proof.text: Put $\kappa=A/(\varpi_E)$. Choose a resolution $P^\bullet\to\kappa$ in degrees $\leq0$ with each term finite free over $A$: map a finite free module onto $\kappa$, then onto each successive kernel, which is a finite set because $A$ is finite. The constant complexes $P_V^\bullet\to\kappa_V$ are resolutions on $V=T,U,Z$ by [lem-constructible-constant-exact]. Their terms are finite sums of the tensor unit $A_V$, hence flat, and [lem-kun-kflat-criteria] (1) makes each $P_V^\bullet$ K-flat. Therefore tensoring a representing complex with $P_V^\bullet$ computes its derived tensor with $\kappa_V$ in [def-kun-derived-tensor].

source.place: ## Proof, constant derived tensor; explicit common resolution for the stalk calculation

proof.text: A closed immersion is finite: on affine charts its quotient algebra is generated as a module by $1$. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] makes $i_*$ exact on abelian sheaves, hence on $A$-module sheaves, since their kernels and cokernels are computed on underlying abelian sheaves. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], its stalk is the original stalk on $Z$ and zero off $Z$; exact stalks and their conservativity [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] show that $i_*$ detects cohomology bounds for complexes. Choose a bounded complex $L$ representing the bounded object $Q$ of Step 2, by good truncation below $a$ and above $d$ of any representative (the truncation maps induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf). In degree $r$ the total complex $L\otimes_A P_Z$ has only finitely many summands, since $L$ is bounded. For each finite free $P^s=A^{m_s}$, the comparison $i_*(L^t\otimes_A(P^s)_Z)\cong(i_*L^t)\otimes_A(P^s)_T$ is the identity on the $m_s$ copies of $i_*L^t$. Additivity of $i_*$ preserves these finite sums, and $A$-linearity preserves the matrices of $d_P$; hence these comparisons commute with $d_L\otimes1+(-1)^t1\otimes d_P$. They give an isomorphism of total complexes, and, by Step 3 and exactness of $i_*$, an isomorphism $i_*(Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z)\cong(i_*Q)\otimes_A^L\kappa_T$. This is the source's closed-direct-image tensor calculation; it uses no coefficient change of $Ri^!$.

source.place: ## Proof, sentence beginning “Exact closed direct image commutes with this constant derived tensor”

proof.text: Tensor the distinguished triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] for $K$ with $\kappa_T$, using exactness of derived tensor [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated]. Step 4 identifies its first term with $i_*(Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z)$. By Step 1, [lem-exc-constant-tensor] identifies its third term with $Rj_*(j^*K\otimes_A^L\kappa_U)=Rj_*j^*(K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T)$; restriction of the common constant resolution in Step 3 gives the displayed equality. Write $H=K\otimes_A^L\kappa_T$. Under this comparison the middle arrow is the adjunction unit $\eta_H:H\to Rj_*j^*H$: its adjoint is the identity of $j^*H$, by the projection-formula definition [def-kun-projection-formula-map]: the tensor comparison is adjoint to the direct-image counit tensored with $\kappa_U$ and $\varepsilon_{j^*K}\circ j^*\eta_K=1$. Compare with the closed-support triangle for $H$ from [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Rotate both triangles so that their first arrow is $\eta_H$; the identities on $H$ and $Rj_*j^*H$ extend by (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to a morphism of triangles. Its third component is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Shifting back gives an isomorphism $i_*(Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z)\cong i_*Ri^!H$, all with coefficient ring $A$. No functorial choice of a cone or identification of connecting maps is assumed.

source.place: ## Proof, tensor the support triangle and identify it with the support triangle of K tensor kappa

proof.text: The forward implication of [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] applied to $K$ gives $H\in D^{[a,b]}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Apply the cohomology-only clause of [lem-exc-closed-amplitude] to $H$, using the original $A$-module vanishing hypothesis. It gives $Ri^!H\in D^{[a,d]}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Exactness of $i_*$ and the isomorphism of Step 5 imply that $i_*(Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z)$ has cohomology in $[a,d]$. Detection of bounds from Step 4 gives the same interval for $Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z$. This step requires no constructibility assertion for $H$.

source.place: ## Proof, first residue test and the closed-support amplitude computation

proof.text: Apply the converse of [lem-exc-residue-tor-test] on $Z$ to $Q$. Its bounded constructibility was established in Step 2, and Step 6 gives the required cohomology interval for $Q\otimes_A^L\kappa_Z$. Thus $Q=Ri^!K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+c+1]$, as asserted.
